title: Your Money and ETFs: Why SEBI Just Made Them Better for You
description: Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) are investment baskets that trade like shares on stock exchanges. They usually track an index, like the Nifty 50, giving you broa.

faq.a: An index is a benchmark that represents the performance of a specific segment of the market, like the Nifty 50 representing the 50 largest Indian companies listed on the NSE.

faq.q: Do I need a demat account to invest in ETFs?
faq.a: Yes, you need both a demat account (to hold the ETF units) and a trading account (to place buy and sell orders) to invest in ETFs.
Most passively managed ETFs generally have lower expense ratios compared to actively managed funds, but the exact fees can vary between different ETFs and fund houses.

faq.q: Can I lose money in an ETF?
faq.a: Yes, like any investment linked to the market, the value of an ETF can go down if the underlying assets or the index it tracks declines.

It means the permissible price range within which an ETF can trade on a given day is not fixed from the start but can expand in stages if the price hits the initial limits, allowing for more flexible trading.
